deferrals.reason: key-dependent effects: for every service_configs entry whose key equals k ignoring ASCII case over its whole length (prop_key_check, src/flb_config.c:782-791), the entry's arm runs: Log_Level sets the log level (:869-894), Parsers_File loads a parsers file (:895-902), Plugins_File registers input plugins into config->in_plugins (:903-908, src/flb_plugin.c:251), every other entry stores one scalar into its own struct flb_config field of its declared type (:909-940); an unknown key only warns (:953); what config retains through a loaded plugin or parser was not read, and v1 cannot state a key-dependent effect

P-FRESH-CONTEXT and P-REGISTERED-DESCRIPTORS: a non-null result is a new context whose config's input list is empty and whose registered input plugins are the build's compiled-in descriptors, one copy each (src/flb_lib.c:145-221, src/flb_config.c:502-507, the generated flb_plugins_register); v1 states the owned result, not a list's contents

Observed at 90978ac6 (src/flb_lib.c:230-263), identical at 046accf6 and 66910c10, read by the rule 10q census: flb_destroy returns at once on a null ctx; otherwise it deletes and frees ctx->event_channel, destroys ctx->event_loop, shuts the engine down when ctx->config->is_running is still true (flb_engine_shutdown) and releases ctx->config (flb_config_exit), then frees ctx. Its own body contains no join and never joins ctx->config->worker; the joins its callees reach are the output and input workers' and, through the chunk-trace pipeline (src/flb_chunk_trace.c:106, :270), another context's flb_stop, which the entry-keyed census cannot tell from this context's engine thread (P-JOIN-IDENTITY). So a destroy while this context's engine thread is live frees what that thread retains: the lifecycle clause L6 (destroy only from created, after a failed start, or after the stop) is a precondition on the caller, not an effect of the body; its admission after a failed start rests on do_start having joined the thread it spawned (L7, checked against flb_start's body). Whether the nullable release of ctx is the whole custody effect (the members it frees, the engine shutdown's own releases) is not derived here.

Read at 90978ac6 (src/flb_downstream_worker.c), not derived by the census: called from one of its own workers it returns -1 without joining (:491-492, which avoids a self join) and without freeing the runtime; otherwise it waits for active operations under the lifecycle mutex, wakes every worker and joins each created worker with the result ignored (:520) before destroying the runtime's synchronisation objects and freeing it. The runtime is freed on that path and not on the -1 return, which v1 cannot state per path.

Read at 90978ac6 (src/flb_input_thread.c), not derived by the census: it copies the input worker's identifier (:591), writes the exit command to the worker and joins it with the result ignored (:607), returning 0. When the command cannot be written it returns -1 without joining (:602-604); whether a caller then releases what the worker retains is not derived.

Read at 90978ac6 (src/flb_output_thread.c), not derived by the census: for each running pool worker it writes the stop command and joins the worker with the result ignored (:646), then destroys the pool (:650). Candidate, not a verified defect: a worker whose stop command cannot be written is skipped without a join (:640-644) and its parameters are freed while it may still run; confirming it needs a native reproduction of the failed write.

key-dependent effects: the tail is read as NULL-terminated key/value pairs, key first (src/flb_lib.c:683-684), each key passed to flb_config_set_property(ctx->config, key, value) in order until a null key or value or a failing key (:691); a key's effect is its flb_config_set_property branch (that declaration's reason); only Plugins_File registers input plugins; whether the value strings are copied on every key's branch is that function's; v1 cannot state a key-dependent effect

Observed at 90978ac6 (src/flb_lib.c), checked by the rule 10q census: do_start spawns the engine thread flb_lib_worker through mk_utils_worker_spawn, which creates it joinable (PTHREAD_CREATE_JOINABLE, lib/monkey/mk_core/mk_utils.c:316-318), and stores its identifier in ctx->config->worker (:973). On both failure returns after the spawn (:980-986, :994-1001) it joins the thread with the result ignored and sets ctx->status to FLB_LIB_ERROR. It returns 0 without setting FLB_LIB_OK when the notification loop finds no started or failed value (:1008). ctx is handed to the engine thread until that thread is joined; v1 cannot state a thread start, a join or that retention. Whether a start after flb_stop can run again (flb_stop destroys ctx->config->cf_main, :1066-1069, and the engine thread's run is not read) is not derived, so the lifecycle permits a start only from created.

Observed at 90978ac6 (src/flb_lib.c), checked by the rule 10q census: flb_stop reads ctx->config->worker (:1047) before its !ctx->config test (:1062), and ctx->config is stored only by flb_create before publication (:174), so the return 0 without a join at :1063 is derived infeasible under P-DEREF. On the FLB_LIB_NONE or FLB_LIB_ERROR status branch (:1049) it joins the engine thread and returns 0 with the join result ignored (:1058). Otherwise it signals the engine to exit and returns the join result (:1077-1083). Every feasible path joins ctx->config->worker and nothing clears it, so the lifecycle permits a stop only after a flb_start that returned 0, once; a stop after a failed start, a second stop or a stop of a never-started context is a caller violation, whose second join or join of an unwritten identifier the native observation reproduced (W47-FB-DOUBLE-STOP-OBSERVATION). The status read (:1049) is not synchronised with the engine thread's own write (:932).
